name: breadcrumbs
summary: The location TRAIL (+ an optional back chevron): a path of crumbs (Reports / Compliance / PCI-DSS Audit) with the current (last) crumb in weight 500 and the ancestors as muted links. Shows where the user is and gives a one-click way up one or many levels. Data-driven `items`; separator is `/` (default) or a chevron. Lives in a page header (obs-page-header has a `breadcrumb` slot). NOT module switching (obs-sidebar), NOT sibling views (obs-tabs), NOT a graph-expansion trail.

variants.name: trail
variants.what: the full path (ancestor links + current crumb, `/`-separated)

variants.name: with-back
variants.what: a leading back chevron before the trail (emits `back`)

variants.name: chevron-separator
variants.what: separator="chevron" → a › icon between crumbs (instead of `/`)

variants.name: divider
variants.what: a bottom rule under the trail (the compliance-breadcrumb header)

variants.name: back-button
variants.what: the smallest atom — a lone chevron-left `back` with a single crumb/title (FlotoBackButton, 3×)

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: font-size 13px; the crumb text scales with it

items.note: the trail — a JSON array of strings ["Reports","Compliance"] or objects [{label,href?}]; or a plain "A / B / C" string. The last item is the current (bold) crumb.

separator.note: the divider between crumbs — any text (default `/`), or `chevron` to render a › icon.

back.note: show a leading back chevron; clicking it emits `back`.

divider.note: a bottom rule under the trail (for a page-header location bar).

events.navigate: ({label,href,index}) — an ancestor crumb was clicked (wire it to your router).
events.back: () — the leading back chevron was clicked (router.back()).

decisionFlow: Show the user's LOCATION plus a way up one or MANY levels? -> obs-breadcrumbs (the trail).
Only need to go BACK one level (a chevron before a title)? -> obs-breadcrumbs with `back` and a single crumb (the back-button atom).
Switch between top-level MODULES? -> obs-sidebar, NOT breadcrumbs.
Switch between sibling VIEWS of the same page? -> obs-tabs.
Put the trail at the top of a page? -> drop obs-breadcrumbs in obs-page-header's `breadcrumb` slot.
A graph node-expansion trail? -> that's a graph-breadcrumb, a different navigator.

trail.useWhen: a nested page needs to show its path and let the user jump up any level
trail.dontUse: a flat top-level page (no hierarchy to show), or for actions (a toolbar holds actions)
trail.example: Reports / Compliance / PCI-DSS Audit — with PCI-DSS Audit as the current crumb

with-back.useWhen: a detail page where a quick way back is as important as the trail
with-back.dontUse: the top-level list (nowhere to go back to)
with-back.example: a back chevron + Inventory / Monitors / web-server-01

chevron-separator.useWhen: the design uses › between crumbs instead of /
chevron-separator.dontUse: when the product's default / is expected

back-button.useWhen: the user only needs to go back one level (the smallest nav atom)
back-button.dontUse: when they need to see where they are or jump multiple levels (use the full trail)
back-button.example: a chevron-left before a detail-page title (FlotoBackButton)

divider.useWhen: the breadcrumb acts as a page-header LOCATION bar and needs a bottom rule to separate it from the content (e.g. the compliance header)
divider.dontUse: an inline trail inside page content (no rule needed)
divider.example: divider → a --border-color bottom rule under the trail

do: Feed the path via `items`; the last item is automatically the current (bold) crumb.
Wire `navigate` (ancestor click) and `back` to your router.
Drop it in obs-page-header's `breadcrumb` slot for a page location bar.
Keep crumb labels short; the current crumb ellipsises if long.
dont: Don't use breadcrumbs to switch modules (obs-sidebar) or sibling views (obs-tabs).
Don't put actions in the trail — a trail is location, not commands.
Don't make the current (last) crumb a link — it's the page you're on.
Don't hardcode colours — the ancestors are --neutral-light, the current is --page-text-color.

a11y.summary: A <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> wrapping an ordered list (<ol>); ancestors are links, the current crumb carries aria-current="page" and is not a link. The back control is a real <button aria-label="Back">. Separators are decorative (aria-hidden). Keyboard: links + the back button are tabbable and activate on Enter.

issues.issue: Ensure a visible focus ring on the crumb links and the back button against the page surface in both themes.

knownIssues.issue: obs-breadcrumbs is a render-faithful reproduction of the product trail (compliance-breadcrumb) + back atom (FlotoBackButton). The real trails are router-bound; wiring `navigate`/`back` to the router is the consumer's. Some product 'breadcrumbs' are actually a back + title/subtitle context header — that pattern is obs-page-header (subtitle + breadcrumb slot), not this trail.

changelog: 2026-07-26 — Docs accuracy pass (owner): added the missing usage card for the `divider` variant (page-header location bar with a bottom rule) and documented the `divider` boolean in the coverage ledger Behaviour section. Reuse/props/a11y verified current. No API change.

changelog.change: Added obs-breadcrumbs — the location trail (+ optional back chevron): data-driven `items` (JSON strings/objects or a "A / B / C" string), `separator` (/ or chevron), `back`, and an optional bottom `divider`. Ancestors are muted links, the current crumb is weight 500 (aria-current). Emits navigate/back. Composes obs-icon. Source-derived from the rendered Navigation/Breadcrumb story + compliance-breadcrumb.vue. Pairs with obs-page-header's breadcrumb slot.
